newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close slightly up, follow Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close slightly up, follow Wall Street.

text.p: Despite several bouts of profit-taking, Thai stocks closed slightly higher in line with a sharp rise on Wall Street overnight, brokers said.
The composite SET index rose 2.70 points to 661.29 on 3.5 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 0.24 point to 48.92.
"There were several bouts of profit-taking during the afternoon session as foreign investors unloaded some communication stocks," said Padermpob Songkroh of Nava Finance and Securities.
Decliners led gainers 159 to 145 while 93 issues remained unchanged.
"The overall market sentiment improved on Wednesday following heavy gains on Wall Street and several regional markets earlier today," Padermpob said.
Brokers said some investors, especially foreigners, sold stocks today as they waited for first quarter earnings of listed firms due to come out next month.
Banks and finance firms released their first quarter earnings last week.
Total net selling by foreigners on Tuesday amounted about 366 million baht.
The banking sector gained most in terms of value, rising 0.65 percent, followed by the communication sector, which gained 1.61 percent.
Bangkok Bank, Thailand's largest commercial bank, topped the active list, falling one baht to 172. Advanced Info Services was second-ranked on the list, dropping six to 174.
The market will be closed on Thursday for the Labour Day holiday. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
